note:
The Mann household at 14 Pelham Crescent (#283) and the Loverseed household next door at 16 Pelham Crescent (#285) on the 1891 return, read from the enumerator's page by A. Hagues. Neither house held any 1891 record before this.

**This answers how the Manns and the Loverseeds are connected: they were neighbours, and the Mann son carries the neighbour's name.** The record has known for some time that John L Mann of 5 North Road was really **John Loverseed Mann** - the 1908 probate notice gave the full form - and that a middle name of that kind is usually a mother's maiden name. Here he is seventeen years earlier, aged 27 and a cashier, in his father's house at number 14, with **Arthur Wellington Loverseed and his family at number 16, immediately adjacent**. See [[mann-loverseed-connection]].

**What that does and does not settle.** It puts the two families side by side on one crescent in one year, which is a far stronger link than the directory's separate entries. It does **not** prove the descent: Mary Ann Mann's maiden name is not on this schedule, and nothing here says she was a Loverseed. Her marriage or her son's birth registration would give it outright. What can be said is that the name did not come from nowhere - the Loverseeds were next door.

**A duplicate to merge before this is run.** The record holds this man twice: **#3306 John Loverseed Mann** (born 1864, died 1908, with the probate biography) and **#3689 John L Mann** (born 1864, same 1901 household). They are one person entered under a census short form. This file binds to **#3306**; the two want joining with the admin page's **Join up people entered under a census short form**, and #3306 still wants renaming to the full form.

**Thomas Mann the father is created here.** He is not in the record at all, although Wright's Directory prints 'Thomas Mann, box manufacturer' on Pelham Crescent in 1894-95, and the firm John Loverseed Mann died as part of was **Thomas Mann and Co. of Postern Place** - so the son went into his father's trade and the father is the founder the probate notice names.

**On the reading.** This is a handwritten page, not a printed transcription. The forenames and ages are clear; **Mary Thraves** the Manns' servant and **Esther Holland** the Loverseeds' are the two surnames I would most want checked against the image before they are relied on. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 14 and 16 Pelham Crescent, read from the enumerator's page by A. Hagues.
